prompt.context: Our client, Classic Bookstore (CB), is a traditional bookstore chain in Spain, specialized in non-technical books. CB revenues have stagnated for the past 3 years, with a stable and loyal customer base. Now, as part of their new growth strategy, they are considering whether to enter the electronic books market. The client is considering selling their own reading devices and developing a website to sell e-books for this device.
prompt.question: Our client has asked us to analyze this opportunity and provide a recommendation on whether Classic Bookstore should enter the e-books and e-reader market.

clarifying_info.a: CB only sells to customers through physical stores; no online business is available.
CB has stores in the biggest cities of Spain.

clarifying_info.q: What types of customers does CB have?
clarifying_info.a: CB has 3 types of customers: Avid Readers (2 books/month), Occasional Readers (1 book/2 months), and Rare Readers (1 book/6 months).

clarifying_info.q: How is the non-technical physical book market trending?
clarifying_info.a: The non-technical physical book market in Spain has been stagnated for the past 3 years.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost of the e-reader device?
clarifying_info.a: CB has reached an agreement with an e-reader manufacturer in China. Total cost per device is 60€. These devices can only support e-books sold on CB's new website.

clarifying_info.q: What growth rate is CB targeting?
clarifying_info.a: CB has no specific growth rate in mind and is open to suggestions.

exhibits.title: Non-Technical Books Market in Spain
exhibits.shows: Two pie charts side by side: the e-books market in Spain (market size 48M€, annual growth 5%) with competitor share breakdown, and the paper books market in Spain (market size 1,170M€, annual growth 0%) with channel share breakdown. Average prices and average annual consumption per reader are also shown.

exhibits.title: CB's Customers Information
exhibits.shows: Total customer count, a pie chart breaking down CB's 390,000 customers by reader type, a bar chart of what customers value most about CB, and a breakdown by reader type of willingness to switch to an electronic reader.

exhibits.title: Electronic Readers Comparison
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of four e-reader devices across price, cost, accepted formats, storage capacity, and extra features.

framework: Market Opportunity: Estimate the size of the e-books market in Spain and assess its growth potential
Competitive Landscape: Identify current competitors in the e-books space and estimate CB's potential market share
Profitability Analysis: Project revenues from e-books and e-reader sales, estimate costs (investment, operating, cannibalization), and calculate profit/ROI
Capabilities & Risks: Assess CB's capabilities to execute (know-how, financials, channel), and identify key risks including cannibalization of paper book sales

questions.prompt: Estimate the size of the non-technical books market in Spain, both paper and e-books.
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure a top-down population segmentation: start with Spain's population (~45M), narrow to reading-age population (15-80), apply a book-buying penetration rate, split by reader type (avid/occasional/rare), derive total books sold, then split by format (paper vs e-book) and apply average prices. Key markers: logical assumptions stated clearly, correct arithmetic, sanity-check of result.

math.setup: Spain population 45M. Ages 15-80 reading target. Split population into quartiles: 0-20 (25%=11.25M, only 15-20 = 11.25/4=2.8M), 21-40 (11.25M), 41-60 (11.25M), 61-80 (11.25M). Total reading-age = 2.8+11.25+11.25+11.25 = 36.5M. Apply 60% book-buying rate = 36.5M x 0.6 = 22M readers. Split: Avid 2M readers x 12 books/yr = 24M books; Occasional 5M x 6 books/yr = 30M books; Rare 15M x 2 books/yr = 30M books. Total books = 84M. Paper (93%) = 78M x 15€ = 1,170M€. E-books (7%) = 6M x 8€ = 48M€.

questions.prompt: Given Exhibit 1, what is CB's potential market share in e-books and what are the revenue projections over 5 years?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note the e-books market is 48M€ growing at 5% annually. CB targets a 1% market share. Candidate must apply 1% to the growing market each year. Additionally, e-reader sales generate profit: 12,000 devices sold in Year 1 (11,000 to switching customers + 1,000 to new), then only new-customer volumes in subsequent years driven by market growth.

math.setup: E-books market Year 1 = 48M€, growing 5% annually. CB market share = 1%. E-book gross margin = 40%. E-reader cost = 60€; suggested price range 60-100€ (margin = price - 60€). Year 1: 11,000 existing customers switch + 1,000 new = 12,000 devices sold. Years 2-5: only new customers (~300/yr based on market growth).
steps: Y1 e-book revenues: 48M x 1% = 480,000€; GM 40% = 192,000€ (casebook uses 190,000€)
E-reader profit Y1 (assuming 70€ price, 10€ margin): 12,000 x 10€ = 120,000€
E-reader profit Y2-5: ~300 new devices x 10€ ≈ 3,000€/yr
math.answer: Year 1 total gross profit from e-books + e-readers ≈ 310,000€ before costs

questions.prompt: Calculate the cannibalization effect: how many of CB's existing customers will switch from paper to e-books, and what is the revenue impact?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 2 to identify switching rates by customer segment. Avid Readers: 97% would switch; Occasional Readers: 4%; Rare Readers: 2.6%. Apply to CB's 390,000 customers split by segment mix. Then calculate lost gross margin on paper books for those customers.

math.setup: CB total customers: 390,000. Avid (13%) = 50,700; Occasional (18%) = 70,200; Rare (69%) = 269,100. Switching: Avid = 50,700 x 97% ≈ 49,200; Occasional = 70,200 x 4% ≈ 2,800; Rare = 269,100 x 2.6% ≈ 7,000. Total switchers ≈ 59,000, casebook uses ~50,000 for simplicity. Avid readers buy 24 books/yr; casebook simplifies: 50,000 switchers x avg books/yr. Lost paper revenue = 50,000 books x avg margin. Casebook: 50,000 books lost x -1.8€ net margin impact = -90,000€/yr.
steps: Avid switchers: 50,700 x 97% ≈ 49,179 (casebook rounds to ~11,000 for device sales first year)
Total customers switching estimated at ~11,000 Avid + smaller segments
Lost paper book gross margin: 50,000 books x 1.8€ = 90,000€ per year

questions.prompt: What price should CB set for its e-reader, and what is the overall 5-year profitability?
questions.guidance: Using Exhibit 3, candidate should benchmark CB's device against competitors. Amazon Kindle (all formats, 750 books, low features) = 100€. CB device accepts only CB-format books, stores up to 1,000, medium features. Candidate should price below Kindle to compensate for format lock-in: 70€ is a reasonable suggestion (10€ margin over 60€ cost). Then compile full 5-year P&L including e-book GM, e-reader profit, webpage investment, general expenses, and cannibalization.

math.setup: Suggested e-reader price: ~70€ (margin 10€). Full 5-year P&L. Webpage investment: -150,000€ (Year 1 only). General expenses: -50,000€/year. Cannibalization: -90,000€/year.
math.answer: 5-year cumulative profit = 342,600€ on a 150,000€ initial investment

brainstorming.prompt: How would you launch the CB e-reader product?

categories.name: Segmentation
ideas: Target Avid Readers first — 97% switching intent makes them highest-conversion segment
Consider loyalty program members as early adopters

categories.name: Product
ideas: Highlight 1,000-book storage and medium extra features vs Kindle's 750-book limit
Emphasize CB's curated non-technical book catalog and customer service reputation

categories.name: Price
ideas: Price at 70€ (below Kindle's 100€) to compensate for format lock-in
Offer bundle promotions: device + 3 free e-books for loyal customers
Volume discount for Avid Readers who commit to a subscription

categories.name: Promotion
ideas: In-store display at all major-city CB locations
Email/loyalty program campaign targeting existing customer base
Social media campaign targeting avid readers aged 15-40

categories.name: Place
ideas: Sell e-readers in CB physical stores to leverage existing footprint
Offer the new website as the exclusive e-book purchase channel
Explore partnerships with Spanish telecom or subscription services

brainstorming.prompt: What other measures could CB implement to increase revenues beyond the e-reader launch?

categories.name: Product Expansion
ideas: Add technical books to the product range to attract new customer segments
Introduce audio-books or digital magazines on the same platform

categories.name: Customer Loyalty
ideas: Create a loyalty/rewards scheme to increase average spending per customer
Develop a referral program to grow the customer base organically

categories.name: Supplier & Device
ideas: Negotiate with the Chinese e-reader supplier to add more formats or features to compete better against Kindle
Explore co-branding or white-label deals with better-spec manufacturers

categories.name: Digital Revenue Streams
ideas: Monetize website traffic through advertising or sponsored author content
Offer premium subscription (unlimited e-books for a monthly fee)

recommendation: CB should enter the e-books and e-reader market. The e-books market in Spain is growing at 5% annually and CB's current paper book channel is stagnant.
A 1% market share yields a cumulative 5-year profit of 342,600€ on an initial investment of 150,000€ — a 2.3x return over the period, with the business turning profitable in Year 1.
CB should price the e-reader at approximately 70€, below the Amazon Kindle (100€), to offset the format-lock-in disadvantage.
risks: Projections rely on a 1% market share assumption and customer survey data; any deviation (lower adoption, fiercer competition) reduces profitability.
Competing bookstore chains could enter the e-books market and erode CB's potential share.
Cannibalization of paper book revenues is estimated at -90,000€/year; if switching rates exceed projections, the impact could be larger.
CB has no prior digital or e-commerce experience; execution risk could hurt both the new venture and CB's valued customer service reputation.
Taxes and time value of money were excluded from this analysis; including them would reduce the real return.
next_steps: Conduct deeper market research and additional customer surveys to validate switching-rate and market-share assumptions.
Pilot the e-reader launch in one or two major cities before full national rollout.
Explore loyalty and referral programs to protect and grow the existing paper book base.
Negotiate with the e-reader manufacturer to unlock additional formats or features, reducing the competitive disadvantage vs Kindle.
